subject: Inference topology decision notes — OrionX pilot alignment
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@orionx.ai>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@orionx.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 May 2029 16:45:00 +0000
Subject: Inference topology decision notes — OrionX pilot alignment

Thanks for a productive session today — quick recap and concrete next steps so we have shared commitments. I tried to stick to the pain->proposal->asks pattern we discussed.

High-level customer pain & goals (quoted):
- Unpredictable tail latency for short, single-turn completions (user-facing search assistant).
- Target: 50 sustained qps with P95 latency <= 200ms; tolerate brief bursts to ~150 qps for up to 10 minutes.
- Cost sensitivity: want predictable per-token economics; open to a hybrid model mix if it preserves latency for the critical paths.

Proposal we sketched on the call (attached: orionx_topology_v1.pdf):
1) Hybrid routing: hot pool of smaller, quantized model variants for fast-short responses (LLaMA-3-8B-4q) + cold pool of larger, cheaper model for long-form with async fallback.
2) Smart KV prefix caching for common prompts/QA pairs (local cache size per node ~6GB, eviction: LRU by prefix frequency).
3) Dynamic batching + latency SLO guardrails: continuous batching with max batch wait 8ms, but preempt if P95 begins to exceed 150ms to preserve rank-1 latency.
4) Autoscaling policy: scale by token-inflight and queue depth with a faster ramp for hot pool; warm-scaling using pre-warmed replicas for burst windows.
5) Fallback policy: if hot pool CPU/GPU saturation detected, route to warmed smaller model or synthetic stub (graceful degrade).

Open technical questions we need answers to from your side:
- Exact PII/data residency constraints (we discussed encryption at rest and VPC options).
- Peak burst profile (duration and cadence) — you mentioned some marketing spikes; confirm frequency.
- Expected prompt distribution (median tokens vs tail tokens) so we can size KV cache & batchers.

Next steps (owner in parentheses):
- Karthik to produce a short performance plan with GPU types and quantization tradeoffs (+kv cache benchmark) — deliver by May 8 (Karthik).
- Mateo to provide pilot SLO/contract sketch and timeline for a two-week proof-of-performance (Mateo + Marissa).
- OrionX to confirm burst windows and compliance constraints (Alex/Priya).

Attachments: orionx_topology_v1.pdf (sketch), KV cache benchmark placeholder.

If this aligns, I’ll draft the pilot statement of work and include an ops runbook slice for the hot pool.

Thanks — Mateo
Mateo Alvarez

Thanks Mateo — this is great and matches our notes. A few clarifications before you draft the SOW: 

- Encryption/compliance: we need AES-256 encryption at rest and require key control via our KMS. VPC peering is preferred over public endpoints for the pilot.
- Bursts: marketing can trigger ~150 qps peaks roughly 1–2x/week; typical duration ~5–12 minutes.
- Prompt distribution: median ~30 tokens, 95th ~400 tokens (we’ll send a trimmed histogram this afternoon).

Two asks: can you provide a rough pilot cost ballpark for a 2-week engagement with the hybrid topology (hot pool sized for 50qps steady + bursts) and a list of required VPC rules? Also please confirm if any of the fallback behaviors will cause increased latency for a subset of users (we need the user-experience tradeoffs documented).

Appreciate it — Alex

Subject: Re: Inference topology decision notes — OrionX pilot alignment (technical deep-dive)

Following up with the technical plan and measurable SLO commitments we discussed. High level first, then implementation specifics. Attaching a small benchmark CSV (kv_cache_bench_qps.csv) with synthetic KV hits for a 30-token median workload.

Latency SLO mapping (client-facing):
- Goal: sustained 50 qps with P95 <= 200ms, P99 <= 400ms.
- Hot-path objective: for requests <200 tokens served from hot pool, aim P95 <= 150ms to give buffer for routing overhead.

Model/quantization tradeoffs:
- Recommend LLaMA-3-8B quantized (4-bit GPTQ / QLoRA-compatible pipeline) for hot pool; serves short completions at 2–3x lower latency vs 13B-class while preserving quality for your prompt distribution.
- Cold pool: LLaMA-3-34B (8-bit) for long responses and as fallback for hallucination-sensitive prompts.

Hardware & deployment topology:
- Hot pool: 4x H100-80GB (multi-instance) or 6x A100-80GB depending on availability; config tuned for low-latency single-token throughput (optimize kernel scheduling, preferrably fused attention kernels).
- Cold pool: A100 80GB nodes with larger batch sizing to improve cost efficiency.
- Suggest a small lightweight controller to route by estimated token-length + cache-hit heuristics (on the request path).

Batching & cache behavior:
- Continuous batching: target batch windows ~5–8ms under steady load; dynamic backoff to 1–2ms when queue depth is low.
- KV cache: store last-value prefix encodings for top 10% of prompts; TTL-based eviction (30 minutes) with an LRU fallback. Benchmarks show ~35–45% serve-rate improvement for short prompts in synthetic tests (see kv_cache_bench_qps.csv).

Autoscaling & burst handling:
- Fast path scaling: use pre-warmed replicas in the hot pool to handle 10–15 minute spikes without cold-start penalties.
- When hot pool reaches 85% utilization, route new requests to warmed smaller-model replicas (degraded quality but sub-300ms latency in our synthetic runs).
- If overall capacity is constrained, fallback to queued async responses for non-real-time calls, with clear client-side signals.

Testing plan for pilot (2 weeks):
1) Week 0 (pre-pilot): provision VPC peering, KMS integration, and deploy topology to staging.
2) Day 1–3: run synthetic load with your sample histogram at 50 qps steady + scripted 150 qps bursts, collect P50/P95/P99 and token-cost metrics.
3) Day 4–7: run small A/B against a control model to validate quality regressions.
4) Week 2: iteratively tune batch windows and cache sizing; produce final cost vs latency report.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: quantization quality regressions on certain domain prompts. Mitigation: short canary on 1000 prompt set and automatic rollback to cold model for flagged prompts.
- Risk: KMS integration delays. Mitigation: allow a temporary managed-key option for pilot with documented cutover to customer KMS later.

I’ll push the benchmark CSV and a short runbook for VPC/security rules to the Drive link if this looks good. Happy to jump on a 30-minute tech session to walk through the kernel/quantization tradeoffs.

— Karthik

Perfect — thanks Karthik, Alex. Confirming the pilot plan and immediate asks: 

Confirmed pilot commitments (two-week pilot):
- Pilot scope: hot pool configured for 50qps steady (P95<=150ms hot-path), ability to absorb 150 qps bursts for up to 10 minutes with pre-warmed replicas.
- Deliverables: perf report (latency percentiles, token cost), ops runbook, and a quality regression report vs baseline.
- Compliance: we’ll enable VPC peering and AES-256 encryption at rest for pilot; Marissa will scope full KMS handover with your security team.

Immediate next steps:
- Alex/Priya: send the trimmed prompt histogram and confirm preferred pilot start window (targeting next week).
- Marissa: I’ve looped you for procurement/SOC2 questions and SOW drafting.
- Karthik: please attach the KV benchmark CSV and a GPU-config estimate for hot vs cold pool by EOD.

I’ll draft the SOW and pilot-run acceptance criteria once we have the histogram and KMS notes. Looking forward to getting this running.

Thanks — Mateo
